alignments.note: Explanatory conjunction rendered by the verse-opening *For*.
Existential verb with the supplied expletive subject *there* riding along as a rule 7 helper; head on the verb word under rule 17.

The negator takes the single English negative *no*. No second negative word stands to carry it, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it, and no quantifier is in question, so rule 87 does not join anything.
Anarthrous noun to its own English noun; the clause's negation stands on the negator under rule 41's test.

Adnominal genitive governed by διαστολή. The ASV realizes that genitive relation with *between*, and a genitive's own case preposition rides with the governed noun where the ASV writes no determiner (rule 21's determinerless clause), rule 17 heading the unit on the noun. One *between* is written for two coordinate genitives, so it stays with the member it introduces, as rule 103 has it for a function word governing coordinate members. Folding *between* into διαστολή's unit as that noun's own English government remains defensible; I took rule 21 because the exception it names is scoped to a frame's *supplied* noun and *distinction* is διαστολή's own gloss.

Rule 70 decides τε by the English alone, and the ASV writes only one English conjunction for τε … καί — the *and* before *Greek*. Under that arm the conjunction is the καί's and τε is its own unrepresented unit, as ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων → *the Gentiles and kings* is. *between* is a preposition rather than a conjunction, so rule 70's two-conjunction arm, whose attested words are *both*, *and*, *whether* and *or*, does not reach it. Reading *between* as the word the ASV wrote for τε remains defensible; I follow the rule's own count of conjunctions. A reference comparison will report this unrepresented τε as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
The καί takes the one English conjunction the ASV wrote for the pair (rule 70).
Genitive noun to the bare English noun, the *between* standing with the first member of the pair.
Second explanatory conjunction to its own *for*.

The article governs the intensive αὐτός substantivally and no noun is expressed in the subject phrase, so the ASV's supplied *Lord* completes the article's own English: rule 102 gives the article the determiner and the supplied nominal together, discontinuously under rule 15, headed on the nominal, and leaves the pronoun its bare *same*. That κύριος stands expressed in the predicate does not make the word `added`: rule 103's test is licensing and not recurrence, and its article carve-out folds a repetition a substantival article governs, as rule 102's REV.11.15 τοῦ κυρίου → *the kingdom* does with βασιλεία expressed in the same verse. Marking *Lord* `added` under rule 103's repeated-predicate-nominal clause remains defensible and is what this verse first took; GAL.3.20 is not that frame, its article governing an expressed noun. Rules 38 and 49 do not empty the article, αὐτός being an intensive rather than a demonstrative, which is rule 38's own contrast at αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ → *that very hour*.

Intensive pronoun to a bare *same*, the article beside it keeping the determiner and the supplied nominal under rule 102. Rule 107 governs a two-word English emphatic such as *he himself*; here the ASV writes only one word for the pronoun itself.
The Greek clause is verbless and the predicate noun carries the supplied copula under rules 53 and 63; head on the noun rather than the auxiliary under rule 17.
Genitive quantifier completing *Lord of all*, with the case preposition riding on it under rule 21's determinerless clause, no article standing to anchor a *the*.

The participle is converted into a coordinate finite clause, so the supplied juncture *and* is a rule 7 helper on the verb it introduces under rule 88, and the copula of the periphrastic rendering rides along; head on the lexical predicate *rich* under rule 17.
Preposition to its own English preposition under rule 36.

Substantival article before a participle with a single English word written for the pair: under rule 90 that relativizer is pronoun and relativizer at once and is the article's, the participle keeping its own verb under rule 32. No head noun is expressed for rule 31 to apply, πάντας being a quantifier.

The particle *upon* realizes the preverb ἐπι- and rides inside the compound verb's unit under rule 106, no expressed Greek preposition standing to answer to it; head on the word glossing the verbal root.
Accusative object to a bare pronoun; rule 106's accusative arm keeps the phrasal particle inside the verb's unit, an accusative having no case for an English preposition to realize.

review_notes: Corrected: t013 *Lord* moves from its own `added` unit into s009's, which now reads *the … Lord* discontinuously under rule 15 and heads on the supplied nominal under rule 102. The competing `added` reading is named in the unit's note.

GAL.3.20 was cited by the earlier note as the identical frame and is not: its article governs the expressed μεσίτης, so the supplied repeat there stands in a predicate slot no token governs. REV.11.15 is the frame this verse matches, an anaphoric nominal folded into the article with its own lexeme expressed in the same verse.
No other unit is altered. All 19 source ids and all 26 target ids remain partitioned exactly once, and the verse now carries no `added` unit.
